title: Cohomology properties of maps in (Cat) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying the 'naive' homotopy category Cat-bar (Cat modulo the homotopy relation generated by the interval Δ1) and the localization Hot(W). He wants to know whether finite (later: arbitrary) sums exist in these categories and whether the canonical functors from Cat preserve them. The previous page made a general remark: a localization admitting a calculus of right fractions commutes with finite limits. This page gives a separate lemma for sums in the homotopy-interval setting.

Lemma. Let (M,h) be a category with a homotopy structure defined by intervals (a 'homotopy interval structure' in the sense of Pursuing Stacks). Assume M has finite sums and that these sums are universal, i.e. stable under base change; in particular I×(∐X_j) ≅ ∐(I×X_j). Then the canonical functor M → W_h^{-1}M commutes with finite sums. Here W_h is the class of homotopy equivalences, and W_h^{-1}M is identified with the quotient category M/~_h.

Reduction. It suffices to show the following. For X = ∐_{j∈J} X_j (J finite) and maps f=(f_j), g=(g_j): X → Y, we have f ~_h g if and only if f_j ~_h g_j for every j.

Proof.
- ⇒ is trivial: restrict the homotopy along the inclusions X_j → X.
- ⇐: each f_j ~ g_j is witnessed by a finite chain of elementary homotopies. Because J is finite, one can choose a single ('un même') interval I_N, a concatenation of N copies of an elementary interval, that works for all j. Shorter chains are padded with constant homotopies.
- Universality of sums gives I_N×X ≅ ∐_j I_N×X_j, so the homotopies H_j: I_N×X_j → Y glue to H: I_N×X → Y. ('On gagne!')

Consequence. From this, the sum in M is also a sum in M/~_h:
- existence: lift the components and take the sum in M;
- well-definedness and uniqueness: this is exactly the ⇐ direction.

The next page shows why finiteness of J is essential. Take X_n = point, Y = the infinite zigzag I_∞, and let f_n, g_n be points at zigzag distance n. Then the lengths of the chains of elementary homotopies are unbounded, so Cat → Cat-bar does not commute with infinite sums. Grothendieck then conjectures that arbitrary sums nevertheless exist and are preserved in Hot(W).
errors: Gap: gluing a chain of N elementary homotopies into a single map I_N×X → Y uses I_N×X ≅ amalgamation of N copies of I×X. This requires products with X to commute with these amalgamated sums. Alternatively one can glue the elementary homotopies one at a time, which only uses universality of the finite sum.

Implicit: if the structure has several elementary intervals, one needs a common interval (composite or product) dominating all of the chains. This is fine in the Pursuing Stacks set-up but is not stated.
Implicit: identifying the quotient category M/~h with the localization W_h^{-1}M. This holds when homotopy is a congruence compatible with products, which is standard but not proved here.

ideas.what: In a homotopy interval structure with universal finite sums, the passage to the homotopy category commutes with finite sums, via gluing of componentwise homotopies over a common concatenated interval I_N
ideas.modern_name: finite coproducts in the naive homotopy category / homotopy category of a category with a cylinder or interval object
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; in Grothendieck's framework, Pursuing Stacks and Maltsiniotis' exposition (Astérisque 301)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses homotopy interval structures and the homotopy relation generated by elementary homotopies; this exact lemma may or may not appear there

ideas.what: Failure of infinite sums in Cat modulo homotopy, because zigzag lengths are unbounded (counterexample with the infinite zigzag I_∞, on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: the naive homotopy relation is not compatible with infinite coproducts; the strictly naive homotopy quotient differs from the localization

deep.surprise_reason: A standard, essentially routine lemma about finite coproducts in a homotopy quotient category defined by intervals, of the kind treated in Pursuing Stacks. Only the I_∞ counterexample on the next page is a mildly instructive detail.
